editorial.headline: Religious Affairs Administration Is Reserved for Government
editorial.standfirst: This government activity covers religious guidance and interfaith harmony—and is closed to foreign investment nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the administration of government services in religious affairs. Its scope is public: fostering Islam, Protestant Christianity, Catholicism, Hinduism, Buddhism and Confucianism, with the stated aims of strengthening devotion to God and advancing harmony among religious communities. Government institutions working in religious affairs are the example given in the record.

That framing matters. This is not presented as a private commercial service conducted around religion; it is an area of government administration, encompassing the public work of religious guidance and institutional support. The record does not list any business scales open to registration, reinforcing that this is not an activity described through the usual commercial scale categories.

For foreign investment, the national position is unequivocal: the activity is closed, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. A foreign investor therefore cannot register this activity in Indonesia as a PMA business. Bali reaches the same practical result: it is closed to PMA registration there today. The Bali restriction is not attributed to the province-wide moratorium for low and medium-low risk activities. Instead, the record identifies the activity as medium-high or high risk and says the position should be verified for the relevant address. That address-level verification does not alter the stated Bali status; it is part of applying the record carefully in a specific location.

The clearest reading is therefore institutional rather than entrepreneurial. Religious-affairs administration sits with government functions, while foreign investment is closed off nationally and remains closed in Bali. Any assessment should preserve that distinction and avoid treating a government remit as though it were an ordinary private-sector registration opportunity.
